meta.title: Browse your memory: pages, history and search
meta.description: Inspect memory pages, backlinks, mail, history and session replay in a browser. Account controls and root proposal review are also available.

hero.title: See what your agent remembers
hero.lede: Browse projects, pages, agent activity, token usage and inboxes in the built-in web UI. Page content stays read-only; authorized users can queue or edit messages waiting for agents.

home.title: Every project at a glance
home.lede: The dashboard shows visible projects, sessions, captured events and compiled pages. Hook-health counters report accepted and dropped events since the server started.
home.shotAlt: Screenshot of the 3.3.0 memory dashboard with project cards, capture counts, hook-health counters and a sidebar for inbox, search and documentation.
home.shotCaption: The built-in dashboard separates captured work from compiled pages; a project can have recent sessions before it has wiki pages.

project.title: A project: its pages, its decisions, its mail
project.lede: Project tabs separate Overview, Agents, Token usage, Sessions and Knowledge. The overview shows captured activity, compiled pages and pending mail.
project.shotAlt: Screenshot of the 3.3.0 project overview with tabs, session and page counts, token totals and a mailbox panel.
project.shotCaption: Select a tab to inspect agent activity, response usage, sessions or the page tree. Missing token reports show a dash, not a guessed zero.

page.title: A page, and what points at it
page.lede: A page shows its outline, backlinks and citations alongside version-specific evidence, declared contradictions and expiration context. History keeps earlier versions.
page.shotAlt: Screenshot of a 3.3.0 knowledge page with an evidence panel, Markdown sections and a sidebar of citations and backlinks.
page.shotCaption: Evidence and contradictions belong to the displayed page version; the browser does not independently verify whether a source is true.

search.title: Search that ranks like the agent
search.lede: Project search uses the same ranker as memory_query. Kind and tier filters apply before ranking, and Explain ranking shows why a page surfaced. Cross-project search uses full text.
search.shotAlt: Screenshot of the 3.3.0 search page showing a scoped rate-limit query, kind and tier filters, and results from synthetic demo pages.
search.shotCaption: The scoped search uses the project’s retrieval stack. Results still need a person or agent to judge their meaning.

graph.title: How the pages connect
graph.lede: A map of the links between pages, drawn by the server. No JavaScript, and no graph database behind it: the edges are rows in the same index the search reads.

items.title: Across projects
items.text: The Graph link in the header draws every resolved link whose two ends sit in different projects, with a table of those edges underneath. It is how you notice that the API project cites a decision taken in the frontend one.

items.title: Inside one project
items.text: Each project has its own map of its live pages and the links among them. Above 120 pages it keeps the best connected and the most recently updated, so the picture stays readable.

items.title: What the launcher is running
items.text: A separate page lists managed runs and their state: live, interrupted, finished, empty. It shows counts, never checkout paths, lease owners or transcript content. Root only on a shared server.

history.title: History, replay and health
history.lede: Three views for the question “what happened here?”

items.title: Page history
items.text: Every stored version of a page, newest first, superseded ones included, with a diff between any two. A version a concurrent write replaced stays visible.

items.title: Session replay
items.text: A project lists its recent sessions, and each opens a timeline of its observations in capture order. With JavaScript, a slider and the j and k keys step one at a time.

items.title: A health page for root
items.text: Hook counters since the server started, the writer queue, the spool, the consolidation queue, the embedder and both providers. Anything failing is listed with the command that fixes it.

readonly.title: Browse pages and review proposals
readonly.text: Edit wiki pages through agent tools, the CLI or Markdown files. The browser can queue or edit a message while it is still waiting; it never claims that message for an agent. Root can review proposed page edits. Database-user grants govern project access; trusted proxies enforce their own authorization.
readonly.api: The same data is available as JSON under /api/v1, and serve --enable-api mounts the API without the browser UI.

faq.q: Is the web UI on by default?
faq.a: The serve command leaves it off unless --enable-web is set. Services installed by setup enable the wiki browser. The separate management console needs its own build feature and runtime flag.

faq.q: Can I edit a page in the browser?
faq.a: There is no page editor. Use memory_write_page, the CLI or the Markdown file. Root can approve or reject pending edit proposals in the browser.

faq.q: Who can see what on a shared server?
faq.a: With database-user accounts, restricted projects are visible to root, their creator and users with a read or write grant. Another operator’s session timeline stays hidden; health and pending views are root only. Trusted-proxy deployments must enforce access at the proxy.
Page content renders without JavaScript. Sign-in, password changes and proposal approval use JavaScript, as do replay controls and theme switching.

management.title: Optional management console
management.text: /manage brings user administration, session inspection and personal MCP keys into the browser. It requires both a build with management-ui and --enable-management-ui at startup; the standard release Docker image does not include it. Users can purge exactly owned sessions in projects they may write; admins can purge any session. Build and deployment guide.
management.keys: Password resets and disabled accounts end browser sessions, but do not revoke self-issued API keys. Revoke those separately. Session purges can leave earlier content in git history, backups and native transcripts.

items.title: Response usage
items.text: Claude Code and Codex hooks report response token use. Project and session views filter by model, harness and tool; older or unsupported sessions show no count.

items.title: Messages waiting for agents
items.text: The inbox shows received and sent mail without claiming it. With write access to both projects, you can address a message to a registered harness and edit it until an agent collects it.

items.title: Guides inside the server
items.text: Feature guides and release notes are bundled in the binary under /web/docs. The guides show what is installed for your account without exposing admin settings to other users.
